- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak forecasts by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction until 2–3 days after sentiment turns.
- In absence of strong sentiment, model should not overreact to short-term volatility — use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecasts.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model should adjust downward by 2–3% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong upward trend, reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overestimating continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply downward bias of 1–2% per day for 5 days.
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome with neutral sentiment, increase forecast by 1–2% per day for 5 days to avoid underestimation.
- When sentiment is positive but true outcome is flat or declining, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day for 3–5 days to avoid sentiment-driven overcorrection.
